claims.claim: Global data center power demand is projected to exceed 200 gigawatts by 2030, and campuses are scaling into the hundreds of megawatts and beyond.
claims.episode_span: global data-centre power demand projected to exceed 200 gigawatts by 2030
claims.source_title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
claims.supporting_quote: Global data center power demand is projected to exceed 200 gigawatts (GW) by 2030.

claims.claim: Scott Hart of NRG said data centers traditionally were 20- to 40-megawatt grid-connected sites, cloud campuses reached about 100 megawatts, and talks have moved to a gigawatt and beyond, against utility planning horizons of 15-30 years.
claims.episode_span: data centres were traditionally grid-connected 20- to 40-megawatt facilities, cloud campuses then reached about 100 megawatts
claims.source_title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
claims.supporting_quote: “Traditionally, data centers would be a grid-connected, 20- to 40-MW facility,” he said. “Then we saw the cloud campuses in the 100 MW range, but now conversations have pivoted to a gigawatt and beyond.”

claims.claim: AI workloads are driving typical rack densities from roughly 10-30 kW into 80-150 kW, with advanced deployments approaching 1 MW per rack.
claims.episode_span: typical rack densities from roughly 10–30 kilowatts into 80–150 kilowatts, with advanced deployments approaching 1 megawatt per rack
claims.source_title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
claims.supporting_quote: AI workloads are driving typical rack densities from roughly 10-30 kW into 80-150 kW, with advanced deployments approaching 1 MW per rack.

claims.claim: Kleyman said 69 percent of AFCOM State of the Data Center 2026 respondents expect rack density to increase sharply, and liquid cooling adoption is showing 36 percent growth.
claims.episode_span: 69 percent of respondents expect rack density to increase like nothing seen in the past, and liquid-cooling adoption is showing 36 percent growth.
claims.source_title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
claims.supporting_quote: “Sixty-nine percent of respondents to AFCOM’s State of the Data Center 2026 survey expect that rack density is going to increase like nothing we've seen in the past,” Kleyman said. “In parallel, we are seeing 36% growth in liquid cooling adoption in data centers, and that's continuing to expand.”

claims.claim: Kleyman said a standard rack can hold six DGX-class systems, each with eight H100 accelerators, and individual accelerator cards cost up to $40,000.
claims.episode_span: a standard rack can hold six Nvidia DGX-class systems, each built around eight H100 accelerators, with individual accelerator cards costing up to $40,000
claims.source_title: The 200 GW Moment: Reinventing the Grid for the AI Economy
claims.supporting_quote: He noted that a standard rack can accommodate six such systems, each built around eight Nvidia H100 accelerators, with individual accelerator cards costing up to $40,000 .
